title: The $1M Singles Tax Nobody Calculates
hook: There's a tax on being single that nobody put in the tax code — but living alone costs over a million dollars more than being partnered, and most people never do the math.
angle: Not just 'living alone is expensive' — the structural, multi-category financial penalty for single people: housing per-capita gap, married filing jointly tax savings you never get, insurance surcharges. Quantified over 30 years into one brutal total.
audience: Single adults 25-45, especially career-focused people who plan their finances solo
key_numbers: $1M+ lifetime singles penalty vs. partnered households
$400K more in housing over 30 years (100% rent alone vs. 50% split)
$12,500/year married filing jointly tax advantage ($375K over 30 years)
$3,400/year average insurance surcharge for single people
54% of US adults now live alone — highest share in history
